title: EMI-LTI: An enhanced integrated model for lung tumor identification using Gabor filter and ROI
author: J, Haw, et al.

steps.title: Download and prepare dataset
steps.instruction: Download the IQ‑OTH/NCCD lung cancer dataset from https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/hamdallak/the-iqothnccd-lung-cancer-dataset?-Resource=download (1190 images, 140 cases, three classes: Normal, Benign, Malignant). Merge the Normal and Benign classes into a single non‑malignant class, yielding two classes (malignant, non‑malignant). Split the data into 80 % training and 20 % testing sets.

steps.title: Apply Gabor filter
steps.instruction: For each image, apply a Gabor filter with parameters freq = 5, sigx = 0.25, sigy = 0.25; compute the absolute value, then normalize to 0‑255 using filtimg = (filtimg‑np.min(filtimg))/(np.max(filtimg)‑np.min(filtimg))*255 and convert to uint8.

steps.title: Segment lungs using contours
steps.instruction: Segment the Gabor‑filtered image by: (1) converting to grayscale, (2) applying adaptive thresholding to obtain a binary image, (3) finding contours of bright lung areas, (4) selecting the largest contour, (5) computing its bounding box, (6) adding a fixed padding, (7) clipping the coordinates to stay within image bounds, and (8) cropping the lung region.

steps.title: Sharpen cropped images
steps.instruction: Apply the sharpening kernel Sharpkernel = [[‑1,‑1,‑1], [‑1, 9,‑1], [‑1,‑1,‑1]] to the cropped ROI using a filter function (e.g., sharpimage = filter(inputimg, ‑1, Sharpkernel).

steps.title: Organize sharpened images
steps.instruction: Further crop the sharpened images as needed and save them into separate folders for malignant and non‑malignant samples for downstream classification.

steps.title: Configure data augmentation
steps.instruction: Create an ImageDataGenerator with the following parameters: rescale = 1./255, rotation_range = 20 ° for the CNN pipeline (10 ° for the EIM‑LTI pipeline), width_shift_range = 0.1, height_shift_range = 0.1, zoom_range = 0.10 (10 %), fill_mode = 'reflect', validation_split = 0.2, horizontal_flip = True. The generator will apply these transformations on‑the‑fly during model training.

steps.title: Build CNN architecture
steps.instruction: Construct a CNN in Python 3 with the following layers: Input 300 × 300 × 3; Conv2D 32 filters 3 × 3 + ReLU; MaxPool 2 × 2; Conv2D 64 filters 3 × 3 + ReLU; MaxPool 2 × 2; Conv2D 128 filters 3 × 3 + ReLU; MaxPool 2 × 2; Conv2D 256 filters 3 × 3 + ReLU; MaxPool 2 × 2; Flatten; Dense 512 units with ReLU, L2 regularization λ = 0.01, Dropout = 0.5; Output Dense 1 unit with sigmoid activation.

steps.title: Set training hyper‑parameters
steps.instruction: Compile the model with Adam optimizer (learning rate = 0.0001 for the architecture description, but experiments used a constant learning rate = 0.001), batch size = 64, loss = binary cross‑entropy, and enable restore_best_weights = True.

steps.title: Train CNN with augmentation
steps.instruction: Fit the CNN on the training set using the ImageDataGenerator defined earlier, reserving 20 % of the training data for validation. Perform 5‑fold cross‑validation: split the dataset into five folds, iteratively use one fold as validation and the remaining four as training, and record per‑fold accuracies (98.63 %, 98.18 %, 98.17 %, 98.63 %, 97.71 %). Overall cross‑validation accuracy = 98.27 %.

steps.title: Extract CNN features
steps.instruction: Create a feature‑extraction model that outputs the activations of the second‑last layer (layer ‑2). Use this model to generate feature vectors for all training images (traindata) and validation images (valdata).

steps.title: Train linear SVM
steps.instruction: Instantiate scikit‑learn's SVC with kernel='linear'. Fit the SVM on the CNN‑extracted training feature vectors and the flattened training labels (use ravel() to ensure a 1‑D label array).

steps.title: Evaluate model performance
steps.instruction: Compute the following metrics on the test set (or validation folds) using the standard formulas: Precision = TP/(TP+FP) × 100 %; Sensitivity/Recall = TP/(TP+FN) × 100 %; Specificity = TN/(TN+FP) × 100 %; F1‑Score = 2·Precision·Recall/(Precision+Recall). Record training loss, training accuracy, validation loss, and validation accuracy (e.g., CNN with Gabor filter: training accuracy ≈ 96.19 %, validation accuracy ≈ 95.48 %, learning rate = 0.001).

steps.title: Test on balanced unseen data
steps.instruction: Download a separate balanced set of 50 malignant and 50 non‑malignant CT images from https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mohamedhanyyy/chest-ctscan-images?resource=download. Run the full EIM‑LTI pipeline (Gabor pre‑processing, segmentation, sharpening, augmentation, CNN feature extraction, SVM classification) on this set. Report confusion matrix (TP = 42, FN = 8, FP = 0, TN = 50) and derived metrics: Precision (malignant) = 1.0, Recall (malignant) = 0.84, F1‑Score (malignant) ≈ 0.91, Precision (non‑malignant) ≈ 0.98, Recall (non‑malignant) = 1.0, F1‑Score (non‑malignant) ≈ 0.98.
